CLIENT PRIORITY #1 (21 Nov 12:35, verbatim): "prio, ensure bagian ini sama kaya di design, gini yaa, color dan reflectionnya". THIS PART = the lake under the sculpture: the concentric ripple rings, the near water and its glint, down to the rocks. It must look like the design in COLOUR and REFLECTION. The client chose YOU (Claude Fable 5.2) for this after two rounds failed (21 Nov ~20:30: "gas, ripple pake fable 5.2").
TARGET: MAIN/notes/round11/refs_user/ripple_target_2026-11-21.png (the client's crop, 1037x325 = the Figma box x325 y524 w762 h239 of the 1440x766 frame, = F000's bottom centre); REF ref_F000.png, loop_F000..F120 (how the rings move).
GROUND TRUTH (read its README FIRST): $SP/work_p4/rip2_gt/ - a Cycles render of the artist's own scene at the engine's REST_CAMERA, F000's wave frame, the Figma box: gt_full.png (2x, 128 spp, looks like the target) and x1/ (1x, 64 spp) with linear multilayer EXR passes (Combined, Depth, Emission, Environment, Glossy Color / Direct / Indirect, Normal) for 4 variants: full, wave0 (Wave modifier off), bump0 (the 'Procedural Water Surface' bump off), hero0 (rings, orb, shards hidden); wave_slopes_F000.json (normal tilt per radius band). Its decomposition: TROUGHS = Glossy Direct = the darker, saturated Nishita WORLD SKY ~45 deg up (linear 0.161, 0.255, 0.551) seen by the wave flanks that face the camera - the cobalt is the sky, not a tint; CRESTS = Glossy Indirect = the low horizon's geometry (snow, floes, mountains) on the back flanks; GLITTER = the ORB (and the ice) reflected through the crests' flanks + the bump's facets (gone in hero0 and wave0), mint / cyan-white; the BUMP makes the facet strokes inside the bands (bump0 = smooth 'mercury' rings). The .blend water is a pure mirror (Principled metallic 1, white, roughness 0.0345, no Fresnel falloff); glossy rays skip the visible sky card (BG.001) and see the Nishita world. Blender 5.2 is available (copies only, through the slot, never save over a repo .blend; rxb's unzipped copy and script: $SP/work_p4/p4rxb/blend/, $SP/work_p4/p4rxb/tools/gt_rip.py) if you need more passes / frames (e.g. another wave frame for motion, or a 1440x766 full frame).
WHAT FAILED BEFORE - read, do not repeat: round 1 (LANES/p4rip; MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/p4pri/{p4rip,judge_p4rip,rejudge_p4rip}/) painted the troughs by ring phase -> flat posterized 'painted' bands, white 'mercury' glint blobs, then a dim grey-mint smear; round 2 (MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/p4pri2/: explorer A = LANES/p4rxa 'MAIN up' (pick winner, then finisher + judge FAIL + fixer), explorer B = LANES/p4rxb 'Cycles GT' (thin regular CG bullseye rings, weak glitter), pick/, judge_p4rxa/): A got the trough HUE right (cobalt, sat 0.35) but reads as 2-3 smooth painted stripes with crisp edges, no facet texture, a soft sheen instead of granular glitter, paler water; a 'calm' that cut the bands at hard lines; a ring-field swap at every press / release. The lead looked at every sheet and agrees with those judges. MAIN (int3) reads more natural than every lane so far: soft grey rings with texture - but not the design's cobalt / glitter.
THE LEAD'S DIRECTION (verify, then decide yourself): make the look come from the physics the GT shows instead of painting it: per pixel, the water normal = the Wave crest train (z = 0.226 exp(-(2.362 a)^2), 2.717 m apart, 1.115 m/s, centre Blender (0, 8.6), Blender front 5.98 m at F000: crests at r 1.90 / 4.62 m) + the material's fine bump (facets; band-limited, mipmapped / footprint-filtered so it cannot alias), reflect the view ray, and take what that direction sees: the Nishita sky's radiance at its elevation (darker, saturated, NOT the pale visible card) for upward rays, the scene / mirror target (horizon geometry, the hero, the orb) for low rays - so troughs turn cobalt, crests silvery, the bands get facet strokes, and the orb's glitter appears on the facets where the GT has it. Check each component against its pass (Glossy Direct vs your sky term on the troughs, Glossy Indirect vs your mirror term on the crests, the glitter vs hero0's difference, the strokes vs bump0's difference) at the target zoom. Start from int3_base's Water.ts (MAIN); you may port any part of A's lane (LANES/p4rxa, its patch vs int3_base and HANDOFF) that you judge right (e.g. its single ring field through press / hold / release, its near-water hand-back), and nothing you judge wrong. Files: world/Water.ts, world/LakeMirror.ts and pipeline/RenderPipeline.ts if the reflection needs it, HeroEngine.ts small hunks. Never edit hero/IceMaterial.ts.
ACCEPTANCE (the client's eye decides; the lead looks before anything merges): side by side TARGET | GT | LANE | MAIN (:5179) at the target zoom (DPR 2 of the Figma box) and at 1x vs F000, at >= 3 clocks (t 100, 100.6, 101.2), plus a 2x glint crop and a 2x band crop: at a glance the lane must read CLEARLY closer to the target than MAIN - 4-5 wavy cobalt bands with silvery crests across the ring field, facet strokes inside the bands, granular cyan-white glitter in the middle under the sculpture, the water tone like the target (zone mean 157,174,198 at the target zoom; troughs 110,137,175 sat 0.375; cyan-white px ~3000), nothing painted, nothing CG, no seams. If it does not, you are not done: say so honestly. Save the final sheets also as MAIN/notes/round11/refs_user/rip3_*.jpg.
HARD GATES (re-run every one on your FINAL build; numbers in HANDOFF): (a) ?p4rxf=0 restores :5173 exactly (ident: final image + all targets + all programs, 20 moving frames, T1, T2, T0 phone, p04 / p06 / p07); (b) FAIR waterline gate (lead, 21 Nov): the old pop gate compared a lane against a 16-sample GT of an OLD base, so legitimate stronger ripple motion near waterlines counted as 'pops' and pushed round 2 into calm zones and seams - do NOT design around that. Instead render YOUR lane's own 16-sample GT with `zsh $SP/work_p4/gt_new/tools/gt.sh <your port> rxf` (six paths, ~11 min, through the slot), capture your 1x sequences with the same cap.mjs (--rows 380,766, 240 frames, same paths; see gt.sh and $SP/work_p4/p4rxa/tools/popL.sh), and run `zsh $SP/work_p4/gt_new/tools/fair.sh rxf '<your caps dir>/%p_L' rxf`: events >= 6 px per path must be <= int3_base's own (vs its own GT: slow 41, medium 73, fast 62, diag 39, reverse 102, leave 54; $SP/work_p4/gt_new/fair_base.txt) within run-to-run noise (+10 %), and look at the worst events at 3-4x; (c) 60 fps sparkle: 40 consecutive frames at 1/60 s, hero frozen, same clock (shoot_ripple.mjs / shimmer.py / jblipmap.py from $SP/work_p4/rejudge_p4rip/tools): one-frame blips must come from the reference's real twinkle, not aliasing - compare lane vs a DPR-2 2x2-averaged capture of the SAME lane (its own GT) and base likewise; the lane's aliasing excess must be <= base's; (d) nothing outside the lake changes (region means == :5173 within run-to-run noise); the ice rings' LOOK unchanged at rest (the client's decision) - if the new lake changes the ice / orb through refraction, measure it and report it (q00-q03 ring pixels) for the lead; (e) perf: T1 real loop, rest AND pointer sweep, >= 6 VALID interleaved pairs at load < 10 (int2's perfab.mjs, SLOT_BG=0 STRICT=1) <= +5 % vs :5173; (f) press / hold / release: one ring field (no swap), p04-p08 not worse than :5173 vs F358-F460; (g) tsc clean (both configs); 0 console errors.
